findings.title: Do not change notification settings through an unprotected GET
findings.body: The new GET route immediately changes the logged-in user's notification level, and the unsubscribe action explicitly skips the XHR check. GET requests do not require Rails' CSRF token, so another site can navigate a logged-in user to this predictable URL and silently disable notifications for a topic. Serve a confirmation page on GET and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST instead.

findings.title: Handle users without a TopicUser record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, but the next statement unconditionally reads its notification_level. The unsubscribe URL is not tied to the email recipient, so opening it while logged into another account that has never interacted with the topic causes a server error instead of unsubscribing. This action does not track a visit or otherwise ensure a row exists. Handle the missing record and create the preference through TopicUser.change.

findings.title: Record unsubscribe as an explicit notification preference change
findings.body: Saving notification_level directly bypasses TopicUser.change, which sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed. For users whose topic preference still has a nil reason, TopicUser.update_last_read automatically switches the topic back to tracking once the reading-time threshold is reached, even after this action has muted it or set it to regular. Unsubscribing must record an explicit user change so subsequent reading does not undo the preference.
